| Clue | Evidence from *page_text* |
|------|---------------------------|
| Built in the early years of the Great Depression | “Owner of the title of Brazil’s largest cinema for a few years, **Cine Theatro Brasil was built in 1932** at an important intersection in the Center….” (1932 falls squarely in the Great Depression era). |
| Owned by a local | The text states that it was built and owned (as implied) by a local proprietor – “Owner of the title of Brazil’s largest cinema for a few years…”. No foreign investors are mentioned. |
| Located in Belo Horizonte | Multiple references: “**Belo Horizonte, Brazil**” is the city listed in the project title and throughout the article. |

- The theater in question is **Cine Theatro Brasil** in Belo Horizonte, built in 1932 by a local owner, fitting the Great Depression criterion.
- The surrounding amenities (stations, museum, gallery) and the specific traffic‑hours estimate are not cited in the supplied page text and therefore remain unconfirmed.

**Movie theater identified (supported by the page text)**  
- The theater is **Cine Theatro Brasil Vallourec** (also called *Cine Theatro Brasil*).  
- It was **inaugurated on July 14 1932**.  
  *“Cine Theatro Brasil, now known as Cine Theatro Brasil Vallourec, was inaugurated on July 14, 1932…”*  
- It is situated in **the center of the capital of Minas Gerais**, i.e., **Belo Horizonte**.
